text: I came in here and wasn't feeling the greatest. I was just coming to get some food and Kaylee came up and was extremely nice. She had many customers and still was able to talk with everyone and get things done on time. She even came pass and said smile. Things always get better in seasons. Then to watch how she worked in her gifting was good. It actually boosted my mental because I felt overwhelmed but to see how gard she was working gave me drive. I needed this push today. Blessing

Of course its great to be able to indulge in some greasy vegan junk food but I was a bit underwhelmed. Although I like violife cheese it just didn't work in the pizza (sorry but daiya is actually better for this). The most disappointing thing was the sauce. It tastes canned and not authentic. I'm from Brooklyn so we know a little something about authentic marinara! Aside from that, the Philly cheesesteak was just ok (personally I preferred the one at The Tasty better) though my husband did like this one the most...and as an avid chickpea tuna fan I couldn't even finish my wrap. It had olives or something pre mixed in it that gave it a bit of a bitter taste. And finally lets talk about what a hole in the wall this place is. I read that in other reviews but thought it was referring to size - no its quite large just really dingy and grimey looking. Maybe that's supposed to be cool? Honestly I wouldn't even mind if the food blew my socks off which it didn't. However there's a new donut place next door with the best donuts in the world.

$5 delivery fee plus tip for a pizza that didn't leave for delivery until after promised time. No notifications or messages until I called for information- said driver was no show. Plus pizza is barely warm because it was probably made an hour ago.

We went to Eldorado while they were having their 2 for 1 special. So our room for 3 days, 2 nights was $40 during the weekday! Can't beat that! The room is clean -- and small. We reserved the standard room instead of the deluxe. The deluxe would have been much more comfortable. But no one is complaining about the room -- for that price! They also gave us $75 worth of coupons. But for a budget traveler, that coupon book is fairly worthless. You're required to dine or shop at the hotel and it's over priced items. Although they do provide $10 in drinks @ Cin Cin or 2-1 chip money. Wireless internet in the hotel is acceptable. It's just not free. But who goes to a casino to browse the Internet, right?The staff is extremely friendly. We were greeted daily by the security personnel who guards the elevators to the towers. To celebrate the Chinese New Year, the buffet theme was Chinese food. If you're going just for the Chinese food, don't bother. Go for what they they are known for -- steak, pot roast, fried chicken, shrimp, salad, especially dessert!
Worst restaurant ever! The owner charged me more tips on my card than I had given，which is absolutely illegal!!!

Stopped in for a quick caffeine boost after mass at the cathedral, which is right around the corner. Spitfire is a really small place, and even a short line will put you out the door. However, the nice folks inside work quickly, and we were able to place and receive our orders within about ten minutes or so. My cortado was excellent-- rich, smooth, and creamy. At just over $3, a fairly priced drink. I didn't try any of the pastries available at the register, but they had some really great looking coconut cookies for $2 a piece. Great place to stop for coffee if you're visiting the French Quarter!
The food here is so great!! Everything we ordered was delicious. The place was so homey and everyone who works there is so nice. I highly highly recommend.

Love this place!! Never liked the idea of vegan food until I tried this place!! My best friend and I were recommended philly cheese steak empanadas, buffalo chicken tacos and Cubano club slider by the waitress there and they were all amazing. I recommend the same to anyone trying that place for the first time!! Will def go there if I'm ever in Philly again!!

I try not to leave negative reviews -- particularly these days -- and I hesitate with Juniper because the food is indeed quite good. But this might be the most poorly managed restaurant in St. Louis, to the point where I'm just done attempting to deal with it. As I said, the food is good -- if you can get it. The problem is the online ordering system, which is neither updated nor in synch with the kitchen. I spent 45 minutes Sunday sitting in Juniper waiting on a pickup order that they were (1) unprepared to make, and (2) incapable of communicating that they were unprepared to make. Just a gigantic and frustrating waste of time. If this was the first time I'd dealt with this kind of online ordering issue with Juniper, I wouldn't be posting here. Alas. So fair warning: If you order a meal online through this place, you might get it! Or not. As for me, I'll no longer take that gamble.

Had a craving for Mexican food today. Ordered the lunch fajitas thinking that would do the trick. Nope. They might as well have put sawdust between 2 pieces of cardboard because that's how tasteless it was. I don't even know how it could possibly be so tasteless. The refried beans were the most flavorful thing in the dish if that tells you anything. Very disappointed. Still craving GOOD Mexican food.

We were walking through Nashville for a nice breakfast place, when we came upon D'Andrews. Very different from other cafes we had come across, D'Andrews had a open, light vibe, contrary to the heavy, dark atmosphere of a lot of restaurants around. The most windows I had seen in the area for one place. The food was just as good. It was a bakery and there was croissants and pastries, that looked(and tasted) delicious. On top of that, they had sandwiches of equal stature. The bread was soft and the falafel of my sandwich was crispy, and it all went so well together. We were tempted to ask if they were selling their bread. I looked over and saw my parents veggie sandwich. The egg literally oozed out the back, in a way that my dad had been trying to perfect, which says it all. Whenever I am in Nashville again, I will be sure to check this place out for a sweet or savory treat at brunch.

I was in town visiting a bunch of my friends and some of them wanted to check this place out (since it was close to where they lived). we thought we'd give it a try. We all loved it. The food is high quality and very well made. Started off with an antipasti platter and we all loved it. It had lots of high quality meats and cheeses. I tried their spaghetti and meatballs and the meatballs and sauce was so good my friend ordered just a side of that as her meal. We sat at the bar and I had trouble picking out a beer at first but the bartender was very knowledgeable and helped each of us pick out a beer that we loved. The atmosphere is very cozy and warm and the service there was very good and friendly. Came back here the next day with my friends and I tried the sausage and peppers sandwich and my friends ordered a pizza. You could tell that the dough was handmade and fresh. The pizza was awesome! I loved my sandwich. It was very filing and came with a side of mixed greens and grapefruit. My friends loved that it was so close and that we didn't have to drive anywhere too far. If you plan on coming here make sure to get here early! It does tend to get pretty busy! Next time I'm in town I'm definitely coming back!

We ate here for Restaurant week...Food was fantastic it was actually the best steak I've ever had. My 3 star rating is because of the service .The waitress was very nice but she was very slow start to finish we were there for 2 1/2 hours..that was a ridiculous amount of time for a dinner out
The staff is friendly, the music is diverse and always on point, ambiance is neighborly, food is delicious New American classics with a Cajun twist, beer is varied, well selected, and fairly priced.

Well, we'll be crossing that one off our list. We went in for lunch and we were the only customers.Still, it took forever for us to get our meal. By the time it arrived the beef in my Shwarma entrée ( which the hostess referred to as the entry) was cooked to the consistency of hard dry leather served on a mountain of rice which sat on three tiny triangles of tomato. It was not good at all. If I wasn't as hungry as I was after waiting as long as I had, I would not have bothered to eat. They had their chance and blew it.

The ambience, atmosphere and the music make this place truly unique. It's never a dull evening at the restaurant. The food has always been great. I've personally only had the pizza, but what great pizza it was. The wait staff were exceptional. Even on a day when they were busier than usual r waitress provided just amazing service in the bar area nonetheless.Very positive experience and i can't wait to go again.
Yummy donuts at a great price!! $3.50 for 2 donuts and a coffee.Lots of different flavors to choose from and the line moves quickly.

Experiences like the one we had last night just remind me that we should stick to Nashville's long standing best restaurants and not try the newbies when celebrating an important occasion. Went in for my daughters' 16th birthday. My husband picked this place because he saw that there were other locations in the NYC area and figured the food would have to be good. He was also thinking our girls would like the gorgeous and Instagram-friendly decor. I went in expecting a higher-end experience (given the pricy menu), but what we got was a glammed up sports bar for "girls," as my daughters said. Had reservations and was surprised to find the restaurant dead, as this is usually not the case with Nashville's better restaurants. The hostess had her back to us when we entered and in spite of me yelling "excuse me" multiple times, the music was SO loud that she couldn't hear me and was startled to see us when she turned around. These two things, as well as the fact that most staff were unmasked and there are TVs on every surface should have been out clue to exit. But we had to put a deposit down on our reservation, so we stayed. Anyway, on to service. Our waitress left us sitting unattended for 15 minutes. I actually got out of the booth and asked the bartender to put in an appetizer order for us because she was not busy (only 3 people at the huge bar) and we were ravenous. She was super-nice and did this, no problem. Waitress finally came over and was clearly harried and pushy about getting our drink order (Including leaning over me and touching my phone without asking me to pull up the drink list). Later she did apologize about the wait and said that she had tables leaving "all at once". Being that the place was not busy, I'm not sure why another employee didn't help her out. Poor training and management?Ok- now food. It was mediocre at best. The highly recommended steak grilled cheese was so heavy and buttery that my daughter took 3 bites and felt sick. Cajun pasta had an unexpected cheesy base - like a mac and cheese vibe (dish was described as "creamy" and not "cheesy"). Neither ate their food. My husband got short rib pasta, which was unimpressive and tasted like it was made with jar sauce. My risotto was a cold gelatinous blob with overcooked chicken on top (ironically called airline chicken and it tasted like it too!). I did have some reservations about ordering risotto in a glorified sports bar, but at $38 and a guarantee from the waitress that it would be "delicious," I took a chance. I should have followed my gut and got a burger. The only standout thing about the meal were the absolutely delicious tomatoes in my risotto. With all the amazing restaurants in Nashville, we will definitely not be returning here. This is more of a place for drunken bachelorettes who care more about drinks and selfies than decent food. It's the kind of place I'd expect to find on lower Broadway, not out in Nashville proper and I will be very surprised if this place is still in business in three years. Maybe bachelorettes and tourists will keep them afloat, but I don't think they will be able to build a loyal local clientele. We expect better and know that Nashville has some truly amazing restaurants. Unfortunately, this is not one of them. Between ignoring the fact that we were celebrating a milestone birthday, music so loud that conversation was difficult, the mediocre food / service, the pricy menu and the lack of COVID-safe protocols, this will not be on our rotation list.

Came here on a Saturday for lunch and it wasn't busy. The place is small but clean, and I loved that there were lots of open windows especially on a day with perfect weather. The service was 5/10, could have been a little more friendlier. The goods.-Pecan pie. Not too sweet, would have been better ala mode!-The windows? The mediocre. -Oyster Po'boy. Stingy on the oysters, buried in too much (overly toasted) bread. No flavor, no sauces. Get your po'boys elsewhereMaybe their oysters are better? but I probably won't be back for my next trip to New Orleans to find out.
What can I say ? They make the best cannolis around . There is no substitute. The only negatives are it needs to be five times the size it is and needs much better parking.

My wife and I have been to restaurants ALL over the world. I've been to restaurants throughout the U.S. and I am totally speechless, but there is no way at all that I will not tell everyone about this place. Geez, where to begin! We've been to restaurants in New York that have been on the top ten list EVER. This is not about bragging whatsoever. This is about the total and most amazing restaurant experience I've ever had. Thank you so much Toscano. The owner approaches you and greets you, the bartender is genuine and engaging, his perfection at his craft is second to none. Dave you are one awesome fuc#king dude. I can't even begin to tell you how damn amazing the food was. My wife describes it as totally divine. Toscano you will be my #1 restaurant EVER. THANK YOU FOR YOUR HOSPITALITY, YOUR GENUINESS AND YOUR AMAZING FOOD

Covid lunch time takeout write up here. I really enjoy Indian food and was going to be near Laxmi's so I gave it a try . I ordered vegetable samosa and a lamb dish and a goat dish. The samosa didn't seem to be freshly made - felt like they were frozen and cooked up for my meal. The korma was good but nothing like any korma I have ever had before. I liked the goat dish the most - plenty of merat and tasty sauce. Parking can be sub-optimal but didn't have an issue this day. The staff should mask up at all times.

It was a lovely Sunday afternoon in the Big Easy. We went to a brunch spot and the waitress recommended Creole House for fried alligator since HB is MUCH MORE adventurous and open to trying diff cuisines. We were seated and greeted as usual. Ordered 2 hurricanes to start. It didn't taste like it had much liquor but it was still good for me. I ordered the spinach salad. It had pecans, grilled chicken, and green apples. It was super filling and really good! HB had fried alligator and crawfish po boy. I wasn't brave enough to try alligator but he said it was pretty good. @That good o creole seasoning gave it a nice kick". No need to add hot sauce. HB really enjoyed. I tried the crawfish and that was decent. We finished most of our meal and then headed off. Worth trying if you're in the area.

The place serves a mix of delicious Thai, Vietnamese, and Chinese food. Prices are low for the quantity and quality of food you get. Owners and servers are very friendly, courteous, and professional. I ate there two days in a row, once for lunch and once for dinner. On the second day, for dinner, the woman owner asked me why I eat alone and said she needs to find me a girl....that was very endearing. I asked if what I ordered was enough, and she replied laughingly that it was "enough for my belly" ....haha...cute. :) I will be going back.

Good pizza. Great service! I love the concept and that you can pick pretty much any toppings your heart desires without being charged an arm and a leg! This location is really clean and they move pretty fast. I haven't been when it's extremely busy... But I actually don't mind waiting while I build my masterpiece in my head. Once you place your order the wait isn't very long at all.

We have been customers since the restaurant opened. We have seen a steady deterioration of the food and service. Carnitas was fatty, tough and all gristle. Chicken burritos had little chicken and too much refried beans. We ordered 5 burritos and they actually charged us extra for the salsa. Not extra salsa... We will not be back. Annas has evidently become popular and successful and they are now taking advantage of the reputation they established with subpar food and service. Go to Speedy Burrito for better food. Annas is rude & arrogant, need I say more...

The food is so so. The chefs are talented but the table service is horrible. Waited 10 mins for a drink order. 40 mins before the chef came this the table and discovered the waiter had neglected to tell the kitchen about my food allergy. Waited another 5 for a new tray of food. Waiter refilled my club soda with tap water. 15 more minutes passed between end of meal and the check. Don't show up unless you have time to kill.

Still 5 stars!I just wanted to update review because they have resumed serving brunch on Sundays!The service is still some of the best in town, and the atmosphere is perfect neighborhood restaurant that is an easy date night. The happy hour is great for whetting that appetite and getting the evening started.But this review is really just about Brunch! They have added a few platters to the menu for brunch this time around. They sadly don't have the ribbon potatoes as a full serving but the potatoes are still very good. Both of the platters are a great way for two people who love to share and love to have a bit more variety than just the food on their plate. They also have a mimosa special of some sort as well as a really good bloody mary.I've been missing a really stand out brunch place since a few of my regular haunts either quit serving or moved, so it is great to see Feast doing what I love.Can't wait to experience their outdoor space during the winter with the panels up on the patio. Maybe it will be done for the next MBC event in 2 weeks!
Best oxtail and chicken. But what took me over was fried shark! Must try the shark. Get yourself a beef patty and please do yourself a favor and ask for the homemade habanero hot sauce.

They have two sections: one for boiled seafood and another for hot/fried food items. And they also sell Chinese food! This is the true hustle, and I totally respect that.I purchased 3 pounds of crawfish and some corn for $17. I was blown away because back home, crawfish is like $9.99/lb. The crawfish were big, some even huge, and so sweet! They were perfectly spicy from the sauce they were boiled in. Sooo good. We also got some boudin and gumbo! I liked their gumbo a lot. It was packed with seafood and seasoned pretty aggressively, which I loved. The boudin was ok, I like mine crisped up on the outside and they just give it to you boiled which isn't my favorite texture. If I'm in NOLA again, I will definitely come back for the seafood! This seems to be a favorite spot of the locals too, we came on a Friday evening and it was packed!

Okay, so last night I hit the delivery button on yelp and to my pleasant surprise I found this little gem. I read the previous reviews which were mixed but overall seemed good so I perused the menu and set to dialing. The guy who took my order was pleasant and even though I know I had to be driving him crazy with my scatterbrained ordering he did not "accidentally" disconnect the call. (Seriously I couldn't read the numbers on my credit card, and then I had a separate conversation with my dog who wanted to eat the card, and my phone...I would have hung up on me!!)We waited about 35 minutes for our order to arrive which is the exact wait time they told me. And then Angels arias could be heard as we peeked inside the pizza boxes. I ordered a meat lovers and oh my goshness it was so yummy looking! I barely had a piece hit the plate before I was eating it and my tongue exploded with appreciation for the flavors that began dancing on my palate. Then I looked at the pizza I ordered for my husband... The southwest chicken. It was so appealing and I had to steal a piece even though I don't usually care for pizza with barbecue sauce (what can I say, I'm traditional in the pizza sort of way! ). Well slap me healed cause I'm a convert! Seriously this was so Flippin DeeeLish! Spicy barbecue sauce, tender chicken breast, and jalapeño devils that start out mild and then sneak up and stab you with their heat. Oh it was yummy!But wait... I'm leaving out my favorite part. Garlic knots...ohhhhh emmmm geeee! I want more right now just thinking about them. I happen to be the type of person who loves my garlic knots to knot (get it? Knot=not...tee hee...ok I'm done! ) be crunchy. These were perfect chewy little clouds of flavor. Oh so good. Give Dominick's a chance. We don't have enough of these little places that remind us that delivery doesn't have to be dull. I'm glad I found them!

Awesome, eclectic must stop to unwind, refresh and recharge. A great place to get away from the city feel and escape. The small bar is just enough and the crowd is friendly. I wish all of the spaces were open at the time of our visit, but certain sections are closed off seasonally.

Service was ok. I ordered an everything bagel with cream cheese and tomato. Not happy. Soggy bagel, pale tomato, way too much cream cheese (can see how much I scraped off). AND $4.50 for a dinky little orange juice. Unbelievable. Bagel was nothing special, and pretty salty. Overall, unnecessarily disappointing.

Not worth the value that they charge for.Nice atmosphere, but food was not great and took some time to arrive. My steak was not well prepared and was served cold.There are plenty of other options where you can get a better meal for a lot less.

What can i say. Well lets just start of by saying i have a new favorite bbq spot. The ribs were sooo juicy, smoked wings nice a crispy on the outside just like i like mines. And the sides were pretty good as well i had the baked beans which had lil pieces of pork heaven throughout and the potato salad which i hardly ever get when out but surprisingly it was good. Oh and i love how the toast up the buns on the grill amazing. Truly satisfied with my meal. Cannot wait till I return the smoked turkey has sparked my interest.

I think I found my new obsession of 2014: Chinese hamburgers. I had these when I was in China (it's a popular street food over there) and it's just as good as I remember: slow-cooked minced pork on delicious mo bread (a flat bread that's kind of like a cross between naan and an English muffin). They have a spicy pork version and a beef and cumin option -- both are great. I also got the spicy sour minced pork noodles, which was a little too sour for my liking but still very good. The portion was huge, too: it easily could have fed two of us. And it's a steal at $6.95. Service was a little slower than what I'm used to for Chinatown, but the staff was extremely friendly. Overall a very nice option if I'm in the area. I'll definitely be back for those hamburgers, though.

I know a lot of my Yelp friends have been here and I had a chance to "go north" for lunch and wound up eating here. They came out with their chips and salsa. I did not know the red bottle was super hot and the other was mild. I can only tell you the red bottle knocked me out. It was so hot it changed my voice. I know to Stephanie S it was just mild to her. LOL!I had a cup of chicken rice soup that was home made. It had so much chicken in it you could call it a stew. Very good. For lunch I ordered the Birria which is goat meat marinated, boiled, then roasted. It was served with the fried beans and corn tortilla. This dish was more of a soup than a plate. I have read that the food can be bland and goat is the anything but bland. Well after you soak it, boil it and roast it goat is bland this would qualify. It is not as pungent goat I have had in the past. I feel this is one of those 3.5 stars places but the price sure makes it a great deal. The service was good not great but in my opinion what you are going to get in a place like this. So if you want to say you tried goat and have the mildest tasting goat I have ever had this is your place.

What I love most is that I know I can come to Campo and get excellent service. I have a lot of dietary restrictions and the staff is always so accommodating without reservation or judgement. I enjoy coming by myself to sit at the bar or meeting a group of people for a fun night out. The wine list pairs great with the food and I know the experience is always worth it!

its gone down hill for me. They use to serve tamales on weekends, not anymore. The orchata use to be homemade, they switched to some powdered god awful stuff and their prices have gone through the roof. Only gringos without knowledgeable taste buds go here.

I always enjoy New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood restaurant and tend to stick to the same items - I ordered the seafood platter which comes with fried oysters, shrimp, thin catfish, crab cakes, fries, hush puppies and coleslaw ....I've never gone inside and have only used the drive thru and my food is always hot, fresh and tasty my fave item is the catfish as I love how thin it is and the seasoning is quite tasty - the crab cakes are just ok as there's lots of filling so the crab ratio is low - if you order the platter do know it's big enough for two people - I'll continue to come because the price isn't bad and the food is tasty

I. LOVE. PIE. and this place!! I usually dont like cream based pies (except pumpkin) but this place converted me. The chocolate cream pie was amazing, not too sweet (surprisingly) and made even better with the HUGE scoop of ice cream we added. Definitely coming back again ASAP. Also learned of their awesome deals through their website / Instagram! Wed- $14 for a sweet slice, savory slice, and drink Fri- $14 for THREE slices of sweet pies!!Amazing :)

Where to begin. This particular Chuy's has been open for a short time and so there may be some growing pains. But if there are not, they are doomed to fail.The first trip we made to Chuy's a few weeks ago, the wait was 40 minutes for two people. We left.We returned and was told again that there was a forty minute wait. We stuck it out. Turned out to be an hour and ten minutes. Finally seated. Very courteous waiter came to our table. I had high hopes.He took our drink order and disappeared for 20 minutes.A possible manager walked by to see if we needed more water, which had been long dry. We asked if we could get the drinks we ordered twenty minutes earlier. He went to get and two other waitresses delivered. Margaritas with zero alcohol. Seriously now the disappointment was growing. It took an hour to get our food. Ever wait an hour for food with four children? Wasn't pretty.When food arrived it was extremely mediocre.Our waiter eventually returned and did a great job, I just felt whomever trained him did a terrible job. Again, he was courteous and attempted his best.I normally give a poor experience a second chance, but that won't happen this time due to the mediocre food. There's too much competition for this area.

Pretty good pizza. You can tell they use fresh ingredients with every bite you take. Many of the chain pizzas have a flavor profile that gets muddled together, but these pizza ingredients each shine on their own and sing in unison. I ordered a pizza to go and was worried it would lose it's stone oven baked crispness on the drive back to the hotel. Thankfully they place a mesh liner under the pizza to retain the crispiness. Definitely worth checking out.

So I came in for a quick lunch to go. I love African food but I'm very picky on injera. I love this thing its like manna from heaven. I was feeling vegetarian today to lighten me up. This was one of the only vegetarian options open that was close to me so I placed my order. Now I pass this establishment all the time but never really thought of it but once Yelp had it as a suggestion I said why not?. I ordered veggie samosas to tide me over while I drive and a veggie combination plate where I substituted the lentils for spinach, and it also included cabbage potatoes and carrots, and collard greens. First bite into the veggie samosas was heaven. It was just spicy enough for your tongue to know you are alive. Sometimes fried somosas can be dry but this was moist and non greasy tasting. It left your tongue tingling.Now the main thang. The veggie combo plate was heavy even in my Styrofoam container . I opened to a folded injera pocket that filled the container I unwrapped it like a birthday present. It was filled with so much hot amazing food. The lentils spicy and juicy, cabbage thick from potatoes and carrots, and the collard greens cooked to perfection. And the injera OMG it has that pungent taste that I crave. I was literally licking my fingers.I will be back I called Nicodimus and thanked him for giving me life this Sunday afternoon.

Sweet baby, Jilly! You exceeded my expectations. After hearing so much about her cupcakes and seeing her tempting lunches on a TV commercial, we knew we had to stop by Monday. When you first walk in, of course the first thing you notice is the daily selection of cupcakes. I was excited to see they had an Egg Nog Cupcake. I love Egg Nog, so I knew that was the one I wanted. However, we had to have lunch first.Our lunches get two thumbs up, I was amazed at the quality and quantity we received. We started out with the Famous Barr's French Onion Soup, a great start to any lunch. As our sandwiches we selected the Monte Cristo and The Cubano. They were plentiful, and better then some that I have seen at popular Tea Rooms. As we feasted on our fabulous lunch, there was a steady stream of patrons coming in and getting cupcakes. My partner was facing the cupcake bar, and noticed when the last Egg Nog Cupcake was snatched up. He broke the news to me, I held myself together and did not cry like John Boehner. After all there was a Turtle Cheesecake and a Chocolate Orange waiting for us. The cupcakes were moist, rich, full of flavor and not overly sweet. They were just perfect. The staff was fantastic. I kinda hate to use the word "darling", but that is the word that comes to mind when I think of the young lady who assisted us and explained our selections. I also, learned that if your doing lunch, tell them which cupcake you want and they'll set it aside. I never miss out on my first choice again.My 50th Yelp Review - 12/14/2010
The food here was absolutely delicious. I highly recommend their teriyaki dinners. However, the service was far below sub-par. The ride staff is not worth the meal.

Pita Pit is cheap, consistently tasty, and has an online ordering system that makes my life a lot easier. I always order the falafel for around $5. It is cheap, filling, and gets me through the day. The service is always decent and the vegetables reasonably fresh for the cost. I typically come here out of necessity and it serves its purpose!

So perhaps I am a bit biased, being a Pisces.But I loved this place for so many reasons! Tucked away from the heyday of the southern part of the county. Reasonably priced. Great service. Fast and fresh. Small but well staffed and busy clientele for a Monday.There are no two fish about it. This place has got it going on. Next time, I will have to try their tapas menu. I love cultural fusion! This time, we tried the rolls from the $4 happy hour menu. We also got a complimentary appetizer.I'm smitten for real. This Fish will be back!

Was recommended to try Jims by some locals and I was very satisfied! So much flavor and wasn't dry at all! Had the cheese steak whiz wit (best way to have the Cheesesteak in my opinion). Waited no longer than 10 min and that was very impressive as the order before me was $210 worth of Cheesesteaks and hoagies! Employees are extremely efficient. Cash only place.
Watching Euro 2012 - lots on TV's but not that English of you watch the Cardinals when England is playing

Great atmosphere and fun environment. The food was just average (2-3 out of 5). However the kind staff, friendly bartender, and cool environment made for an excellent experience. Overall I give it 4 stars.

Take out was very quick but I think the bang for your buck is with the all you can eat. Sushi was good, not sensational but good variety of fish and combinations so definitely more options to try on future visits. Located in a shopping area so joint parking lot but plenty of spots. Prices were very reasonable and definitely worth a go.
The food is pretty great, the prices are a bit high. Very cute inside and outside.

We've driven by a few times & I suppose we always passed it up because of it's "hole in the wall" look, but don't let it fool you. The food is delicious! The gumbo is awesome and the shrimp in the shrimp plate are huge, and it comes with at least 12! The cup of gumbo was more like a bowl and filled me so much that I ate only 2 shrimp. It's a good problem to have, especially considering how cheap it is to eat here. The server was very sweet. I'm so glad to have finally stopped in and add a new St. Charles Parish food spot to the list (we live here and often run out of places to eat). The hours are also very good, so definitely give it a try.

Awesome beer garden with solid beers and great food. The garlic chicken fingers were amazing and the fries were perfect. Also they had lots of choices for beer and I really liked all if their seating options. Ill be returning to this place all summer.
Great for lunch! You walk up to the shack on the side of a liquor store and they take your order. Awesome authentic food!

It's so gooood. It's not a cheap night- I reserve it for special occasions. But, I also sometimes make-up special occasions so I can go. My favorite things I've had here have been the Verti roll (truffled eel sauce, come on) and the Zahav roll (sushi grade albacore and edamame falafel?!). So creative and fun, but not over the top. I also had a live scallop appetizer once that I still think about sometimes, and the Surfer Roll is amazing. Anyone would like this place: from sushi snobs to squeamish fish eaters. And, no matter what they're doing: they do it well. The fish is super fresh and the flavor combos are so inventive.

Today was my first time trying food here. I ordered honey chicken tenders and fries. First off, customer service was very friendly and polite (also they had great taste in music lol i love the temptations). I got my food pretty fast for just made food and by goly was it delicious! The sauce was absolutely great and the fries were seasoned too! Overall , if i could give this restaurant more stars on their review, I would.

Visited here for the first time. Everything I tasted I enjoyed.I started with the house salad. It was very tasty featuring feta, dried cranberries and a tasty house made vinaigrette. I followed up with the Shrimp and Grits. Solidly the best Shrimp and Grits I have had in TN. My friend had the filet. It was perfectly prepared and the portion sizes were good. We dined at the bar and had a great overall dining experience. I imagine it would be even better at a table on a date.
Food was decent, but over priced and we waited two hours for a table. Our server completely ignored us, drinks where never filled. Not worth the wait at all.

We have been coming here for 20 years and the pastries and quiche are quite good and the period architecture is unbeatable. The only reason it does not get five stars is that the restaurant needs a thorough cleaning from top to bottom!

After reading reviews I had high expectations and our experience just didn't match up. Chips and salsa is a charge. The guacamole tasted like it was grocery store made. The margaritas were super tart and the street corn was literally just a pile of mayo on top. Very disallowing.

Wow where to start. The food here is subpar especially considering the breakfast buffet is $13. There was food on the floor at the buffet that you had to step around in order to get your food. The interesting thing is that the waitstaff appeared to be totally oblivious to this. When I grabbed my first plate I realized that it was still dirty put it down and grabbed the next one. Probably should've just left the restaurant at that point. I certainly would've been better off.The scrambled eggs were over cooked, the sausage was very greasy and there really wasn't much else really edible to me. Coffee was probably the best thing at the buffet only perhaps better than the coffee in my room.Now for the best part. The restaurant uses some sort of dark floor like a wood floor and it was absolutely filthy. I didn't notice this at first or I would've walked right out. I mean you could see every foot print for what appeared to be the past week. If you catch it in the light it almost looks like there's grease all over the floor. It looked like ice at a skating rink.I'd say they probably do the most business at night, specifically because you can't see how nasty the floor is. I'll stick to the coffee in my room and find a better place tomorrow for breakfast.

Just July's was just as good and just as busy as when I visited last year. Breakfast was good and filling! Whether you get the gravy & biscuit, pan cakes, french toast, hash browns, eggs and bacon or a bit of all of it, or any of the other various items offered.... it's all Good! Very popular, very busy place, but very friendly and attentive staff.

I can't believe I discovered this place two weeks before I move from Philadelphia. I would have taken every out-of-town visitor here! The ambiance is incredible - floor to ceiling rugs, cushioned alcoves where they seat your party. It's a great deal at $25 per person with four courses. Plus, it's BYOB. You can't go wrong. Unless you're a vegetarian. I don't know what they'd serve you, since three of the courses revolved around meat.

I love this place for the atmosphere the seating outside is so incredibly uncomfortable I almost don't want to go. It is close to the house, the people are friendly the food is good, hard to talk when the band(s) are playing, but come on upgrade the outdoor seating, its been at least 5 years and counting!!!
Service is always really good, particularly Danielle. Food is what you'd expect but I enjoy going here for a quick bite.

I went to Hawkers for my first time yesterday. My sister wanted to go. Sat at the bar and after a few minutes the bartender took our order. Few minutes later we ordered. That was the end of the bartender waiting on us. Everything else we had to stop them and ask for. Had to stop the bartender in passing to ask for another round. My sister ordered some balls thing. I ordered the wings. I'm a timely manner my sisters food arrived but not mine. She needed a fork but no one seemed to care. The staff was socializing and I finally looked at the guy talking said excuse me and asked for a fork. 15 minutes later still no wings. I told my sister to eat cause I was over it. She asked where my food was and 30 seconds later it appeared. Why 30 minutes to cook wings? The wings were average at best. No one asked how our food was. I had to ask for the check. I do not understand the unattentiveness of the staff. I really wanted to leave no tip but I don't roll like that. The fly's swarming the beer taps were gross as well, beer in a bottle for me. When you have to ask for food, silverware, drinks, and the check it's just ridiculous. I will not be back
Service was excellent food was out standing.

I came in about 30 minutes before they closed and they were ready to shut down. I ordered a grouper sandwich and they asked me what side I wanted with it. It said $13.99 but I was charged over $16.00, so the side must have been extra. I got my food to go and it looked appealing but I ran across several bones in my grouper sandwich...that kinda killed it for me. I probably won't rush back.
Great food, great customer service, the staff was very knowledgeable and helpful. The roasted Mary's chicken was the best chicken we have ever had.

The food was great. More than ample servings. Good service. Who could ask for anything more. I had the Indianapolis (Hand breaded Tenderloin, two scrambled, Sausage Gravy, home fries, and toast). It was super. More than ample serving. As was nice wife's Kansas City(two biscuits with Sausage Gravy, two scrambled eggs, and home fries. Wit crumbled Bacon on top.) We remembered the Oasis at it's former location. The move not only preserved a bit of history, but gave Plainfield a super place to eat. We WILL be back.

Fantastic service.Great food... A small little place you wouldn't expect in the area. The server was fantastic (wish I recalled her name). I would definitely go back to this place regularly if I lived in the area.There is a small bar the locals go to at night to hang out.

Ok, my experience the 2nd time was so much better.The pulled pork is still delicious...The fries aren't that bad...The collard greens are a little spicy...The mac n cheese still isn't my taste.The seating arrangement is solved by sitting outside...Overall, it was a very good experience, although it could be a little better.

The food seems to generally be great, although I wish they had more options for picky people like me. Service is excellent, and the place is small (read: cozy or cramped, take your pick).Disclaimer: I'm not a huge breakfast/brunch person, but my boyfriend is. I'm also not the biggest fan of cold food, read: sandwiches. Therefore, I had a hard time finding something I'd like off Cafe La Maude's menu, but I definitely see the potential for people who like eggs, aren't lactose intolerant, aren't allergic to fruit, etc (I know, I have a lot of problems!).I got the steak frite sandwich, which was pretty good, but nothing to shout about. In fact, the bread was pretty hard and tired out my jaw, so I took half of it home and heated it up--it tasted infinitely better then! I especially liked the combination of steak, avocado, and mustard aioli. The fries were great and flavorful--but not in a normal, salted way! On the other hand, my boyfriend got the french toast (Berrylicious Pain Perdu), and it was so. beautiful. And he said it tasted as amazing as it looked! (Picture posted.) He definitely wants to come back for brunch again.The service was excellent, and everyone was really friendly. They don't really assign a specific server to you, so the waitresses frequently check up on you to make sure you have everything you need--especially before you get your food. When I was there, people came out of the back and talked to customers they seemed to know.The space is a little cramped, and the high-top tables in the front each have a tall chair and a spot on a long booth that goes against the wall. I imagine walk-ins are best for two. Oh, and you can definitely hear everyone's conversations.

Mind blown. My mind is officially blown. This was the best restaurant in New Orleans. I got the collard green melt-the wedge salad and deviled eggs with chicken skins. And I would order that same thing if I made it back in there. Everything was seasoned so perfectly and the atmosphere was so fun and hip and I loved the nice touches they offered . I loved everything about this place.
Pssst.....Chili's fajitas suck in Boise too.Gross chicken, napkin-like tortillas. And something that was supposed to be "beans and rice".Our server was nice though.

I just love this place... the kava is delicious. the kratom bombs are a unique twist that pack a perfect punch. the decor is wonderfully inviting. the people are always friendly and knowledgeable. I have been coming to this place for almost two years at all times of the day or night - whether around lunch time or early in the morning darkness. this is the kind of place for which I have been looking... a friendly vibe and decent people... plus no alcohol.

I really enjoyed this place. It has great quality food and a great atmosphere. I really enjoyed the service and staff, very friendly and helpful. And the customers seemed to be a god mix of locals and visitors. Had the bacon melt( was more like great quality ham), the marinated Brussels sprouts, and a local beer; all was great!

We went to Chambers on a Saturday afternoon and found this place to be a notable stop when we are in the area. Their food was well made and the prices were very resonable for the area. The seats in the booth we had may need a slight updating as the stuffing has seen its day.

The food here was horrible.It was bland no seasoning at all. Great Service nice people but I don't see how they make money I felt robbed ..Was expensive and lacked everything. I don't mind spending money on decent food. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone.I wanted to rate a minus 4stars.
My friends had the BBQ whilst i had desert. They said the ribs were great. My chess cake was AMAZING!!!

I suffered through the wait once with a friend and it was almost worth the wait. Wasn't that busy and still took over 30 minutes to get our meal. The next trip I had to leave because it took so long. 30 minutes and nothing. The final attempt I had arrived alone at 11:20am and asked if I could be seated at a 4 seater since I had my laptop for business. There were only two other people seated. The greeter said no. I said goodbye. Last time I'll try. The only sandwich I had was great. Just trying to get one is tough.

Chilaquiles were delicious. Pancakes were "meh". Otherwise, we ordered a simple eggs and sausages meal for the kiddos and the sausage was there favorite part. Happy campers=happy mom. Make sure you pick up your utensils and napkins if you will need them. Unfortunately, we didn't and since we were staying at a hotel we had to eat everything like cavemen.

I've been here once. It was on a Saturday afternoon and I was craving some hot chicken and noticed the reviews for this place so I went.I ordered the hot chicken breast sandwich with fries. My order came out in less than 2 minutes (highly suspicious me thought it's definitely not fresh). It turned out exactly as I thought. The chicken was fried way earlier and was dry and hard to chew on. Spice - I don't think it was even hot or mildly spicy for that matter. I was disgusted at the end of the meal.For one, I don't think I'll ever go back. For you, get something else besides the chicken. A good question for the staff if you are here would be "what's fresh?"

Great location on the beach. Service was consistently good.Frozen drinks were on point.... Non-alcoholic beverages can be taken out of the restaurant. We loved getting a drink and taking back to our condo pool! Food was just ok.On three visits over the course of our vacation we had:Fried grouper sandwich Coconut shrimp with mashed potatoesHouse salad with ranchConch frittersChicken strips (not recommended)She crab soupSeafood is where it's at here, of course. Come expecting food in baskets, a laid back beachy atmosphere, nothing fancy...Tables were sticky with sunscreen and sand residue, but I guess that's to be expected!We went here 3 times in one week because of close proximity to our condo and the beach. Not sure how this Frenchy's compares to other locations... I'd say this isn't worth a special trip but if you're nearby it does the trick!
I highly recommend this place! It is amazing. My favorite is the rainbow bowl with peanut butter. The people are very nice as well!

Good Food. I just thought the Customer service is above and beyond. Hope to have some food catered for our business meetings. The owner and the rest of the crew were verry friendly and awesome. Enjoyed my lunch.Buffet starts at 11:30- but we arrived early and they hustled to set up everything even though we were the only guests in sight.
Very cool, brewery.. Beer is very well crafted. If you like German style beer they have an amazing selection. Staff is friendly this place is going to need to expand!!

We went to Famous Dave's the first week it opened in Reno. The wait was long, but we expected that. We did head to the bar to dull the pain of the wait.Our wait staff was very attentive considering that we were a table of seven. The food was great with generous portions. The atmospher was very fun....All and all, we had a great meal.

I went to Baja Cafe for the first time today and I was so Impressed! I'm disappointed that I haven't been here for breakfast sooner than today. My boyfriend and I had awesome service, our waiter was so friendly and the food came our super quick. We started off with a prickly pear mimosa and they were delicious and big. Most mimosas we are able to finish quickly, but these were big and filling! I ordered the construction burro with chorizo and other veggies, and my boyfriend ordered the biscuits and gravy combo, we were surprised at how quickly everything came out and how delicious it was. Our waiter knew it was our first time to visit Baja cafe and brought us a complimentary snicker doodle pancake- sweet and delicious! We were so impressed with our entire experience and cannot say enough good things about Baja cafe. From the service, cleanliness and timeliness to the food and drinks we will DEFINITELY be coming back and bringing our friends and family with us! If you haven't tried Baja Cafe yet, you better get over there!
Pretty good burger! Popular place with a decent wait time on a Friday night. Order a Monsoon instead of a Hurricane. Classic New Orleans spot.

Good service, but that's about it. The sushi tastes like it's been out all day and the rest of the food doesn't taste good. The appearance of the food is also bad. Everything looked greasy and messy. I had a hard time putting food on my plate and I didn't even eat it all. It's also kind of expensive. They charged us about $15 per person. That is too much for a disgusting restaurant like that one. I'm very disappointed. I will never crave Asian food again.

One can really taste the star anise in the pho broth. It's nice. I like the onions to be sliced paper thin, but the amount of basil, sprouts, etc. offered are generous. This restaurant is a solid choice for pho. They pack take-out dishes well, too.

I used to drag my friends here regularly for late night bar food because I loved the Pic SO MUCH, but the last two times I've driven the 40 minutes out here have been huge disappointments. Really poor service with one mistake after another.This last time, our meals were served, but our orders were incomplete. The server forgot my friend's celery with her wings (it was specifically ordered and YES, coats extra), which took a grand total of 15 minutes. I was waiting for my crab soup, which i had to remind the server about when the appetizers AND meals were served. When I finally got it, 20 minutes after our meals were first served, it was ICE COLD. Completely inedible.It's sad to say, but I don't think I'll be back. Maybe it's for the best, as the moron at the table next to me was telling his friends, "Ya know, Shakespeare referenced the KKK in one of his plays." Stay in school, kids.

The hubs and I visited Miguel's yesterday after a surprisingly brief visit to the Apple Store. I was really excited to see how busy it was, as I remember that Johnny Carino's was typically a ghost town. As per usual, we found a seat at the bar.We started off with a margarita (strawberry blended) and an order of guacamole. The guacamole had a great texture and flavor, but it was WAY under-salted. As in, I salted every bite before I put it in my mouth-hole. Same thing goes for the chips. The salsa was pretty good, a little less hot than I might like it but I understand that it has to be made for the masses of tender-tongued Reno folk.The margarita tasted great and had a decent tequila flavor, and I appreciate that they take the time to make each margarita individually, rather than having a big machine that does it. There was a mix-up with the drinks but the bartenders fixed it quickly and with a smile. We ordered our food and waited. It seemed like it took a LONG time for the food to come. I didn't clock it, but I would estimate it took about 30 minutes or so. Which, if I'm ordering something that has to be baked to order I can somewhat understand, but Mexican food always seems to come out very quickly. Not sure what the problem was. I ordered a ground beef taco and a pork tamale combo; the hubs got a ground beef chimichanga. Talking about it on our way home, we decided that it wasn't that the food was *bad.* It just didn't taste like anything. I might as well have been eating cardboard. I couldn't pinpoint where the lack of flavor was (I continued to salt), but it's one of the meals that I think wasn't worth the calories. I hope this is just some growing pains, I know they're new, so I might give it a shot after awhile one night when I'm down there for a movie.

I can't say enough good things about Amato Bros. The atmosphere is welcoming, like you're hanging out in a friend's basement bar, but with better food & good drinks. The staff, especially Chris, the bartender/manager, is super colloquial & I find myself excited to see him behind the bar because he's just a cool dude to chat with while we're dining/drinking. There's always a good beer selection, but even the seasonal cocktails don't disappoint. I wouldn't usually trust a gin cocktail to a bar in a hoagie joint, but I was pleasantly surprised to find myself dreaming of English garden parties on a cold first day of winter. My guy ordered a dirty vodka martini on the whim of a craving & it was executed to his taste: not too dirty, not just vodka with some olives. The food really stands out here. The menu is huge (HUGE), & there is something for everyone. I struggle to choose each time I'm in because the chicken cutlet sammies are drool-worthy (my guy literally thinks about them all day), but the hoagies (including the meatless options) are also memorably delightful. Everything is just so fresh, you can tell that this establishment is run by a family that cares about quality & cares about you.

I'm already excited for our next visit! We were promptly and sincerely greeted on our arrival. The hostess was extremely enthusiastic, and made us excited to try everything. The margaritas were outstanding! Best in Tucson, hands down!!! We had the combo tacos, carnitas and mahi. The tacos were so fresh and tasty, . Even though we normally pass on dessert, again that wonderful, up selling hostess suggested we try the churro ice cream sandwich, so we agreed since she hadn't steered us wrong yet. Another homerun on the dessert!! On leaving, the hostess once again suggested we come for "taco Tuesday". We left absolutely content and satisfied, and will certainly be back on Tuesday!

I have never been a fan of St. Louis style pizza which was why I was so happy to learn about Dewey's. They serve hand tossed pizzas with a thin center and a thick, chewy crust that they baste with garlic oil. I have never had a bad pizza from here, no matter what toppings I ordered. They also have a lot of delicious and creative specialty pizzas that break out of the mold of most specialty offerings. An overall great place, great food, great service, great atmosphere. I can't recommend it more highly.

Went to this place for the first time and it was great! The guy with the white hat who cooked the fish and chips did an amazing job. Maybe one of the best fish and chips I've ever had. Great flavor and the chips where hand cut slices of potato. Came with a little garden salad. The environment there is great too. Has a roomy bar/pub feel with booths and pool table but friendly for kids with games, etc. I didn't visit the outside patio but it looks huge and very welcoming. I will definitely be back and will probably try the burger. Support these guys!

We like this place. The people who run it and work there are all very nice, upbeat and professional. The food is good quality and the servings are ample without being those huge platters that no place should be serving. Drinks are well-made. Prices are right on target. We've sat at both deck locations (one to either side of the bar) along the river. Very pleasant. I recommend this place for a very casual, comfortable, outdoor dining experience with well-prepared food and good service. All at a reasonable price.

How can you not love this restaurant.? Had birthday party dinner here , everyone treated us very special! .. The drinks are great and the seafood cooked in a variety of ways are cooked to perfection, the views are awesome too!

Went in and sat down and ordered. Ordered two appetizers and an entree each (3 of us). Ordered a strawberry lemonade. When she brought it out I noticed something white sticking out of the ice. Thought it was a piece of lemon till I realized it was frozen in the ice. Putting it in the light I realized it was a piece of raw meat, looked like shrimp. I told the waitress who took it, didn't apologize and made a joke about it being raw goat. She didn't tell the manager and brought out the appetizers which of course it was mixed up. We asked for the manager who finally came over. His name was Matt.Showed matt the picture since the physical sample was already gone and his response was "I don't know what it is from the picture. I have no way of knowing what it was and hey these things happen you know how it is." No.... No I don't know how it is. I know what guest service is, and I know that wasn't it. He didn't try to take care of us in any way. Didn't reassure us about the other food or say it was their mistake. Didn't own the situation in any way and took zero responsibility.I know what raw meat is and I know what ingesting it can cause especially if dirty and rotting. We told him we were leaving. He said he wouldn't charge us for the food we refused to eat like he was going out if his way to accommodate us.Guest service is terrible, staff was awful and the food.... Well to quote them... They have no way of knowing what it was.

Very prompt and courteous staff. The goat cheese appetizer is unbeatable. For the entree I had a delicious t-bone steak that melted in my mouth. The host Ralph came over to our table checking on our satisfaction and made us feel right at home. We also had 3 kids under 12 with us and the kids menu was a pleasant surprise. Highly recommended restaurant.
I love their pizza! It taste fresh and hot every time we order there! The delivery service is great as well. I always get my pizza within 30 mins or less!
Relaxing, fun atmosphere. Very happy to have a place where I can bring kids for a meal that I too can enjoy amazing food and nice cocktails!
Love that they have a vegan skillet now :) Great coffee quick service! (The avocado is extra)

We stopped here for breakfast one morning while running errands. The food is just okay. The place was busy but it feels and looks dirty inside. The customer service was below average. At the time of our visit, they were having issues running credits cards, so everyone was withdrawing money from the ATM and the line was extremely backed up. I will never come back here again.

I visited Bridge Tap House & Wine Bar when I attended a conference in St. Louis. This is a great gastropub that has a nice atmosphere. The food was good and there was a lot of it. I started with their paprika popcorn and then I had the Cuba, Missouri sandwich with house chips and it was enough for two. They had a nice beer selection and the bartender was very knowledgable.
Service was slow. Topopo salad was tasteless and looked like they threw a bag of frozen vegetables on top. No guacamole. Steak Picasso was not picado, bland. Chips and salsa and waitress were great.

This place really sucks.. I went to pickup food my family ordered. As I am waiting the lady the owner makes a very inappropriate remark about my weight. She didn't know I was pregnant at the time. Regardless what a shitty place where you are not accepted because you are fat. Little did she know I know what she said. Since I speak the same language.

ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS PLACE! the owner is so sweet and the burger has they most amazing taste! Reason: because they make it as if it were a homemade hand pressed patty! The flat bread concept so amazing! Love it here!
Tried the ice cream on a fresh chocolate chip cookie -- truly awesome!! Very friendly staff, good selection, good prices.
This is a very popular spot on a Friday night, and it's probably has something to do with their great beer and relaxed atmosphere. They close relatively early, though (9 PM).

In looking for a sushi restaurant in the area, I read a few of the reviews for Maru Sushi. I decided to go there for my birthday dinner. I was not disappointed. The sashimi was fresh and had good size pieces. We also had the Naruto Kiku roll, the Jimbo & the Bloody Mary rolls. Very tasty!! The correct amount of rice and nice portion of fish. We have found our new sushi place for the Boise area!

Stopped by while on vacation. Initially thought they were closed because sign had not been flipped. Extremely glad we did not drive away. Though difficult to get to and is abit rough looking on the outside the food is beyond worth it. I had the mumbo gumbo and the boudine balls. Was easily the best we had on our entire trip. As a chef myself I can say you should make the time to stop by Chef Ron's. You will not be disappointed.

This was my first time here. Heard lots of reviews by people I know so I took my mother and a friend tonight. Had reservations for 8 pm. Parking was easy. The place was decorated nice and the drinks were good. We all ordered a different plate to try each other's meals. Had a huge problem with the service. The waitress took forever with the drinks !!! There was only one bartender working on a Saturday night with a live band event ? It was horrible. I had to get up and ask for our drinks 2 times. The waitress was at the mercy of the 1 bartender. Not to mention our waitress was a mess as well ! She messed up our order 3 times. I ordered 2 sets of appetizers and she brought out one of each ! Then apologized and brought out my appetizers with the main course ? We sat there with no water,no drinks,and all wondering why we were thirsty during our diner. Sad to say I wil not take the trip again. The taste of the food was good. The service made us all upset. ISLA VERDE YOU NEED MORE BARTENDERS AND SERVERS WHO LISTEN TO THE PEOPLE PAYING TO EAT THERE! Was a 250+ bill and wasn't a good time.

It's a very modern rendition of "dim sum". Actually, it shouldn't even be called a dim sum place at all because the name is quite misleading. It's more of a sit down and order from a menu kind of restaurant. Yes, the portions are smaller like typical dim sum, but I refuse to believe this is a dim sum place because where is the DIM SUM CART? The service was wonderful and the layout is nice. I like how they have that little peep window so customers can watch the chefs at work. The food was decent, but not extraordinary. Their first downfall was that they did not have chicken feet. I was in shock, what kind of dim sum place doesn't have chicken feet! The scallion pancakes were delicious, but you have to dip it in the dumpling sauce, that's the trick. The pork soup dumplings were flavorful and steamy. I was disappointed that they didn't have the mild vinegar to pour over the soup dumplings. The vinegar on the table was way too strong for my liking. The shrimp dumplings were probably the worst. It tasted straight up like the frozen stuff I can pick up at the Asian grocery stores. The outer wrap did not have that nice consistency, but instead fell apart like old dough. Overall, I thought the food here was okay, but there are a lot of glitches. In terms of food, they have the concept, just poor execution. This is not your traditional dim sum, probably a more contemporary spin.
Best place in the world for gelato! If you don't believe me, check National Geographic. I'd recommend the mojito flavor, though it is not always in stock.
Ive only been here a few times and that's because I live so close to the bakery but it is by far the most expensive Cuban bakery I've ever been to!!

I've visited Sentinel Peak three or four times since we've moved to Tucson. It's been good enough to return but not outstanding. Part of the reason we return is they make a very good Bloody Mary...my wife's criteria. The menu is bar food but for the most part is good in that regard. The beers have been uneven. I've had some exceptional beers there...but they've been one-off's, it seems, because I've never seen them offered again. My benchmark beer is an IPA...it's the first thing I order at a first visit...Sentinel Peak's has been a bit uneven...sometimes it's a 4/5, sometimes a 3/5. We'll be back but I think there are better overall operations in town

Service,Food,And drinks all GREAT!!I had a reservation for two on a Friday night at 8pm and was immediately seated as soon as we arrived. They immediately took our drink order and brought out bread.I ordered their 'Manhattans' as my drink and I must say,boy was it not only delicious but it was STRONG! I appreciate heavy handed bartenders and whoever the bartender was,was definitely heavy handed. They were amazing and very reasonably priced.For an appetizer we had the calamari which was perfectly fried and comes with two sauces. The bread for the table included very warm and soft bread and some like pizza shops that both were good.I also had the Caesar salad which was standard but good.For my entree I had the shrimp & lobster fettuccine.It was rich,creamy,flavorful,and had sufficient amount of lobster and shrimp in it.So I give this place 5 stars and looking forward to going back to try some of their other dishes

We enjoyed dinner at the Walnut Street Supper Club before a show at the Walnut Street Theatre on a Wednesday night. The restaurant was not that crowded but starting to fill up when we were leaving. Our whole group loved everything about this place. Great 40's atmosphere, our waiter was a dynamite server as well as great singer. Love the whole concept of the wait staff also being entertainers. Food was delicious especially the goat cheese appetizer and the lamb chops. We will be back again !!

This is by far the best food I have had in the Nashville/Clarksville area. I am from California and am out here because my Fiance is in the Army. We are both very used to the luxury of amazing food in northern Cali. We have been to many restaurants looking for great food. We found it! The decor is awesome, very cute and artsy. The basil lemonade and pomegranate-pineapple red tea are SO tasty and refreshing. We ate the Zipper and the T-bird sandwiches. They were amazing! I cannot say enough good things about this place. We were stunned with how good everything was. From the beginning to the end our entire experience was a great one!Thank you Silly Goose for a fantastic lunch!

We always sit at the bar... The bartenders are great! If we are just gonna go hang out somewhere and have some laughs this is our first choice. Prices are reasonable, staff is nice, food is Applebees.
This place is the best! Absolutely amazing service and staff every time I go there. The food is always good and consistent no matter what you order.

Came to philly from out of town and went to this restaurant. I must say that at first I was a little bit concerned given the overall look of the restaurant when walking in. But man was I sadly mistaken because when we finally were able to sit down for a meal I can easily say it was one of the best meals I've ever had. There are not many places that I would gladly spend $400+ dollars, this restaurant clearly is one of the few. Will be back!!!The tuna, steak, peppered cauliflower, and full chicken were fantastic!!!!

I was working in the plaza last week and needed to get some lunch. After checking out their menu I was more torn than before, they have a lot of tasty sounding options. I decided to stick to a basic cheeseburger with hand-cut fries and it was really good. I was starving so I inhaled it but aside from being overcooked the meat was good and veggies were fresh. I was a little disappointed in my drink though. I ordered a strawberry lemonade and for $3.50 you get a smallish cup with chunks of strawberry in fake lemonade. I was impressed they used real fruit but if you're going to go that route why not make the lemonade fresh too? Especially for that price. Either way I look forward to trying out more of their food soon.

We always come here whenever in Reno. Good food and good service. They recently added burger with foigrass. What a treat. Shrimp scampi is served table side. Steak are always cook to perfection. We eat so much and dont usually have room for dessert. But they always provide complementary to go dessert (coffee cake). That's a nice touch. Will always come back when in town.

I am giving this place a two stars mainly because the food was good, the lovely couple I was conversant with and the decor of the facility. Needless to say, I will never come back here again!!!Business owners must realize that customer service is key to bringing customers back.1.) I came in and was greeted by the manager, however when I sat at the bar, I waited almost 10 mins to be acknowledged by the female bar tender 2.) The bar had less than 20-25 people and a few people in the dining hall, the bar tenders were running around like the place was packed3.) The female bartender did not offer me a menu and did not state the happy hour specials (I had to request these items)4.) I order the berry drink and it was awful, I told the waitress about it and ordered a new drink, she did not take the berry drink off my bill and told me that she would have to charge me for the martini, I was appalled because I never assumed that I would not pay for my drink, the way she said it was almost an insult.5.) I ordered wings (in which the bar tender ordered me chicken tenders instead and insisted that, that is what I said, but any who) which I asked for fire engine hotness and they wanted me to sign a release waiver not to sue!!!! So I changed my order to hot, I was not going to take that chance!!6.) The apple martini I ordered was in a stingy martini glass and tasted lack luster. And the drink was $9.50 and the booze was premium shelf!!! The local hood bar, will give you top shelf for $2.00 less..I will never come back, this is sad because my girl friends were waiting to hear about my experience so they would try this restaurant and bar. Needless to say they will not be trying this establishment.
Really good and you get a metric ton of food. The sauces are all very good, and everything tastes very fresh.
Great meal for a great price. Fed 4 of us drunks for $22... say waaaaaaahhhGet the 4 sampler
Everyone loves sonic. It's one stunk. Te ones down south were awesome. This one ehh

My family and I stopped by the downtown location on Magazine St. The food was alright, the wait a little long, but my service from Jimmy was great. He was fast, efficient, polite and knew exactly how to handle the "family with kids" type of table.Will be back again!

Was looking for a cheap quick place to grab a bite- and after reading the reviews, decided this was it. Boy, what a mistake that was! The appetizer my boyfriend and I shared was decent, however the chicken & shrimp I ordered was disgusting, had no flavor and was extremely chewy. The mashed potatoes weren't even that appetizing. I was incredibly disappointed in this restaurant - although it was fairly busy for a weeknight - so perhaps I just ordered the wrong meal. I do not think I will be visiting Moe's again, although the Simpson theme is cute.
Great happy hour, one of my favorites!! The kale and popcorn is amazing and I'm not evens fan of kale! Ate the shrimp and corn pizza and was great!
Great Food Wonderful Staff Everything on the menu is Delicious FREE LIVE MUSIC ON THURSDAYS!!

This is a great sub shop- I would choose it any day over Quiznos or Subway. They have a huge variety of toasted subs. The service is always fast, and they have funky fun decor. The guys who run the place are almost always on hand and super friendly. A great place to stop for a quick lunch!

Good customer service, short waiting time, clean establishment, very nice atmosphere, slightly above average burger , great fries but if you decide to get the cheese on top of the fries be aware of the dissapointing cheese.

Oh. My. Goodness. This place has awesome steak tacos. They also serve chile rellenos which is really good too. My work buddy raves about the chicken quesadillas. The only problem is that there is generally only one waitress during the lunch hour. She sometimes runs like a chopped-off-chicken-head, chicken.

This place had some amazing chaats and lassis. We got bhel Puri, garlic and ginger chicken chaat, chicken green chili chaat, rose lassi and Pina colada lassi. The chaats were delicious and the spice level can be customized to your preference. The rose lassi was really good.. it's made out of fresh roses. The owner is super friendly and the service is good. Would definitely recommend!
Piquant Is a French bakery, bistro with a wonderful atmosphere. Although on the pricier side, it is well worth it. The service is always great, the food is delicious, and we always enjoy it!

The food was ok. The service was absolute garbage.My wife and I stopped off cuz we were hungry. I ordered a bacon cheese burger with mushrooms and fries on the side and she ordered Philly cheese sandwich and mashed potato.I received a mushroom burger fries and gravy and my wife received Philly cheese sandwich and fries.Yes...the gravy was on my bill. I didn't touch it. I hate gravy...and my wife was looking forward to the mashed potato but she never eats fries... i would have mentioned it to the waitress had she actually spoke to us during the meal at some point, and I had to chase her down so I could get the bill.If this place mailed me a $100 gift certificate i would throw it away. Bad service. Terrible
The food and prices are fair, but with so many comparable places in the neighborhood it is subpar. The meat was somewhat dry and was lacking some spice and flavor.

Went there this past Saturday with family. They have a very extensive menu, which is good. But the wait for the food was a little long. The food was OK. If I was going to give advise, it would be just go for dessert. Like I said, the food was just OK, but the desserts really were superb. The waitress made us wait a long time and the food was not worth the wait.

We arrived and waited a few minutes to be seated. Then waited several more minutes to be greeted. This isn't usually an issue, however, with so many staff standing around, it felt like we were being intentionally ignored. This may not have been the case, just what it felt like.We ordered water and a Diet Coke. We were given a sprite and water. One of the glasses had lipstick on it. At that point we decided to just get chips, salsa and queso. The server swapped out the sprite can for Diet Coke. The chips were thick and delicious. The salsa and queso tasted great too, however the overall impression encouraged us to leave as soon as we could. Too bad, because it's location is a great spot if you're doing any kind of touristy stuff downtown.

Last night, I had the pleasure of attending a media/influencer night preview HOTTEST new gem in Ybor City, 7th And Grove. Bringing you a modern flare to southern comfort food, is Chef James Roberts. He is the head chef and truly the epitome of someone who is passionate for what they do. The way he carried himself and the way he spoke about his food was all you needed to know about him.You can truly tell Chef James very much so enjoys what he does. I had the chance to chat with him for a few moments and when we spoke about the dishes he prepared for us last night, he said to me, "I'm not just a chef, I'm a craftsman," and that resonated deeply with me. July 26th. That's NEXT Friday folks! Mark your calendars. 7th and Grove will open their doors to the general public! I'm telling y'all. You're gonna want to make sure you check this place out. The decor, the cocktails, and the food are a WHOLE ENTIRE VIBE!

Great happy hour. Perfectly shucked oysters. Seriously, not one grity sea booger and I've ate here countless times. I am huge liver pate enthusiast. Luke has the best I've ever had. I usually go for oysters, pate, and a few drinks so I can't comment on the entrees. Service is wildly inconsistent. On one occasion it was truly terrible. The manager noticed without us complaining and comped several drinks and dessert.

This place has the BEST tacos. There are so many authentic Mexican restaurants in Tucson, but this one is by far my favorite. I came here looking for a quick bite to eat and asked Rachel about her favorites on the menu. I got the taco special and was not disappointed. 10/10 would recommend to anyone who needs something quick but unforgettable.
cool atmosphere, delicious vegetarian salad, fun sitting and eating at the bar - all great!!the keg wine is good but should be at least $1 or $2 cheaper.
